notes: P3.3 quoted sha256 679fe331... as the pin for artifacts/candidates.jsonl. That pin in release/MANIFEST.jsonl is STALE and was stale before this branch: the artifact moved 679fe331 -> b74576fa (3de10b7) -> 5113ad32 (c6a5b82), and c6a5b82 is an ancestor of this run's base. The condition read literally was unsatisfiable when written; it was scored on intent (E15 must not move the hash) and passes -- 5113ad32 stable across four regenerations. The stale pin is a live manifest-stale break for the release track and was reported, not touched.

A mutation battery running in this shared worktree left live mutants in tracked source during the run. Two subagents reported phantom suite failures (13 and 2) caused by them. All numbers here were taken on a tree verified clean by git diff immediately before and after.

The three *.stdout.txt captures were normalised to LF before hashing: .gitattributes pins LF, so hashing the working-tree CRLF bytes would have recorded sha256s that no committed blob has -- the same defect as the stale release pin reported above, and it would have been self-inflicted.

M30 was a real survivor and was acted on rather than filed: the success/status disagreement guard was one-directional. status==0 with success false fell through to result.x and minted a Certificate from a failed solve, which check_exactly would then report as a CertificateError -- i.e. as weights that failed re-checking rather than as a solve that never succeeded. Guard made symmetric; the refusal carries a rebuilt undecided outcome so a caller cannot read decided=True off a refusal. M30 and M31 (the one-directional variant) are now both killed.

An earlier MUTATION.json reported 30/26/4 with M30 as a SURVIVOR, three minutes before potential.py closed that hole, and nothing on its face said the counts were stale. An adversarial review caught it. Regenerated (31/28/3) and mutate.py now stamps the HEAD and the dirty state into a `tree` block, so a stale report can be recognised as one.

tools/check_status_bit exited 1 under a reverted engine by raising AttributeError before it could print a verdict, and main() built its report list eagerly so N1 crashing meant N2 never ran. Both fixed in af884509; NONVACUITY.md's table is corrected to say so. The exit code was always right; what was missing was which property broke.

STATUS_MEANINGS[no_linear_pagoda] and LpOutcome.no_linear_pagoda's docstring said HiGHS 'proved' the LP infeasible and that no such weight function 'exists'. That was the only unhedged existence claim reaching an emitted artifact while the 'floating point, no Farkas dual' caveat lived only in Markdown. Both now say 'reported' and name the missing certificate.
